title: Creative AI across capture, performance and editable production
summary: Today’s expanded research covers 53 creative fields, including a new neural-camera field. It completes earlier screened guides and adds researched discoveries across media and physical practice. All entries distinguish reviewed software licenses from models, assets and services; no discovered software was installed or run. A focused ComfyUI result review retains Ready to try because the available exact-model preference chart lacks enough evaluation context to verify creative output. The library gains 39 distinct tools; 16 earlier screened entries become full guides. Metadata beyond the README shortlist and the retained historical backlog were reviewed in bounded passes; other raw matches remain private for later screening. Any failed requests and bounded queries are disclosed in the execution summary. Codeberg and SourceHut access was recovered through public endpoints after initial browser failures; all eight configured ecosystems have researched findings. The neural-holography PDF exceeded the fetch size limit, and some project pages could not be retrieved. GitLab repository documentation was retrieved through its API. Model metadata and downloads were discovery signals, not permission to include unreviewed software.

Reviewed implicit surface recovery, motion-aware material simulation and procedural assembly authoring. Exported geometry is not automatically fabrication-ready.
Reviewed browser creative interfaces and agent workspaces. Conventional creative-coding frameworks were not assumed to be AI tools.
Read current immersive-web development guidance and Quest camera sample documentation. Host SDK terms and on-device validation remain separate.
Reviewed neural codecs and agent-authored procedural assets. Deterministic rendering can be part of an AI workflow without itself being learned inference.
Revisited biosignal-conditioned art and open real-time signal infrastructure. A signal-processing platform does not by itself prove a learned creative behavior.
Reviewed parametric CAD, neural inverse knitting and assembly authoring. Geometry validation and machine-readable labels do not guarantee a successful physical fabrication.
Reviewed engine authoring and editable asset generation. Public alpha claims and large tool counts do not qualify as independent quality evidence.
Reviewed learned dance generation and geometrically grounded text-to-motion research, retaining dataset and body-model dependencies.
Completed earlier virtual-performer and Maya bridge guides. The xiaoke.ai homepage is a directory rather than a verified companion-app demo; character and voice assets retain separate rights.
Reviewed video relighting and controllable video manipulation. Unreleased larger models were not treated as available functionality.
Reviewed SoundSpaces and neural acoustic fields. Geometry-based acoustic simulation and learned acoustic reconstruction are distinct operations.
Expanded capture into lensless and event-camera reconstruction, with hardware-specific input requirements.
Reviewed agent video-production sites and relighting tools; local project storage does not establish local inference.
Revisited VFIG and animated explanatory diagram tooling. Learned SVG generation differs from deterministic drawing operations.
Reviewed modal typography research. The Strike a Chord page still marks code as forthcoming, so it was not admitted as released software.
Searched narrative video and comic production. Comic Sol distinguishes released deterministic mechanics from unfinished live AI integrations.
Reviewed presentation tooling and comic export. An image-based PDF does not establish accessible text or screen-reader support.
Reviewed unconventional capture and neural restoration. Synthesized detail must be distinguished from an observed photographic original.
Reviewed AI-assisted cartography and explanatory animation, keeping generated factual/spatial claims subject to review.
Revisited projection and biosignal art, and researched trained-scene display on lenticular panels. Hardware calibration remains workflow-specific.
Expanded into learned telemetry sonification, dance and virtual performers. No live latency or audience study was conducted.
Expanded textile design and inverse-knitting research. The INTEX project page describes a recommender, but its published homepage still needs an implementation audit before inclusion.
Reviewed sonification and AI-assisted visual interpretation. A demo or a generated narration is not a substitute for user testing.
Reviewed Android diffusion distribution and headset camera inference. Device support must be established for the particular app/model combination.
Revisited creative-ML curricula and interactive teaching tools; a curriculum is not automatically a standalone AI application.
Reviewed score recognition and pottery digitization. Recognition or generated reconstruction requires comparison with the original artifact.
Added neural-camera practice to the effective plan and followed adjacent textile, haptic, scent and display research. Unreleased work remains outside eligible additions.
Revisited text-conditioned vibration generation. The Tactus site could not be retrieved, and software/weight permissions require distinct checks.
Read primary neural-acoustic-field and sound-space descriptions; no claim that all acoustic simulators themselves use AI.
Reviewed cross-stage agent production for video, audio and 3D. Proprietary hosts, model services and local editor code are separately identified.
Revisited modal typography and animated diagrams. Release availability and concrete learned behavior remain eligibility conditions.
Completed a music-to-dance guide and revisited text-conditioned motion. Research outputs do not establish retargeting quality or real-time performance.
Read the cooperative embroidery paper and screened actual inverse-knitting code. Knit-by-Command currently offers goals and placeholder usage rather than a documented implemented AI workflow.
Completed earlier optical score-recognition guides and revisited multi-track symbolic generation. No recognition accuracy is inferred from source availability.
Reviewed the released Lumen 1.3B route separately from unreleased variants and editable material research.
Revisited the Anemoia scent project. The reviewed page did not establish a new complete, openly licensed application to add.
Reviewed instruction-driven interior layout and procedural assemblies. These outputs do not establish architectural compliance or physical correctness.

Researched DirectL display integration and neural point light fields. The Princeton page was forbidden and the neural-holography PDF exceeded the fetch limit; those gaps are not presented as completed paper reviews.
Reviewed agent-driven Maya rigging and virtual performers. A generic Foton page yielded no substantive content; performer-asset permissions remain separate.

Reviewed editable assembly generation and CAD agents. Recorded-response tests do not establish live prompt reliability.

Revisited FRIDA robotic painting and embodied creative systems. Installation demonstrations do not transfer hardware validation to other robots.
The ToonComposer page returned no substantive text in this retrieval; adjacent controllable video research was reviewed, with that access gap retained.
Reviewed official video-to-audio documentation and neural speech cleanup. Sound-generation rights and expressive-voice preservation need separate checks.
Revisited CoolChic setup and lensless audio/image encoding. Encoding or reconstruction claims were not accepted as cryptographic guarantees.

Revisited Timeflux and Mind Draw Play. Biosignal-conditioned art is not evidence of validated thought decoding.
Reviewed editable neural material programs and USD agent assignment. Learned generation and deterministic material assignment are identified separately.
New configured field: researched event-to-video and learned lensless reconstruction, including camera calibration, optical measurements and simulation routes.
